raw_answer_text:
A1: The first 32-bit word contains the Source Port field (16 bits) and the Destination Port field (16 bits).
A2: The Sequence Number normally identifies the sequence number of the first data byte in the segment; when SYN is set, it instead represents the Initial Sequence Number (ISN), and the first actual data byte would be ISN+1.
A3: The Acknowledgment Number is valid only when the ACK control bit is set; when valid, it contains the next sequence number the sender of the segment expects to receive.
A4: Data Offset specifies the length of the TCP header, measured in 32-bit words; its minimum valid value is 5, corresponding to a minimum header length of 20 bytes.
A5: The same word also contains a Reserved field (3 or 4 bits depending on the spec version), the Control Bits/Flags field (6 to 9 bits, e.g., URG, ACK, PSH, RST, SYN, FIN), and the Window field (16 bits).
A6: The checksum covers the TCP header and TCP data, plus a pseudo-header consisting of the IP source address, IP destination address, protocol number, and TCP segment length (fields taken from the IP header, not part of the actual TCP segment).
A7: The Urgent Pointer is only meaningful when the URG control bit is set; when valid, it indicates the offset from the Sequence Number of the last byte of urgent data, marking the end of urgent data in the segment.
A8: The Options field appears only when the Data Offset value is greater than 5 (i.e., header length exceeds 20 bytes); the maximum total TCP header length, including options, is 60 bytes (Data Offset value of 15, 15 × 4 bytes).
